case_title: Prabhu Chawla v. State of Rajasthan & Anr.
neutral_facts: The case involves a dispute over the interpretation and application of Sections 397 and 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. The accused filed petitions under Section 482, which were dismissed by the High Court on the grounds that an alternative remedy under Section 397 was available. The Supreme Court examined the validity of this reasoning and found that the availability of Section 397 does not preclude the exercise of inherent powers under Section 482. The Court held that the High Court's order was contrary to the law and remanded the matter back for reconsideration under Section 482. The case highlights the interplay between the revisional powers under Section 397 and the inherent powers of the High Court under Section 482, emphasizing the need for self-restraint and the importance of securing justice.
